stem: A mechanical model reproduces a ventricle ejecting through a semilunar valve. Investigators narrow the valve opening while keeping the initial filling load and contraction strength fixed. Which of the following changes should the model show?

options.text: Higher ejection load; smaller residual volume
options.explanation: The outlet narrowing does increase ejection load, but the residual-volume prediction is reversed. Greater resistance to emptying leaves more blood behind at constant contractility.
options.label: A
options.misconception: Assumes that increasing the opposing ejection load leaves less residual blood at fixed contractility.

options.text: Lower ejection load; greater residual volume
options.explanation: The residual-volume direction matches impaired emptying, but narrowing the outlet raises rather than lowers the opposing load. Both parts must fit the mechanical intervention.
options.label: B
options.misconception: Treats narrowing the outflow opening as a reduction in the load opposing ejection.

options.text: Lower ejection load; smaller residual volume
options.explanation: This pattern would fit easier ejection through a less restrictive outlet. The model instead narrows the semilunar opening while holding contraction strength fixed.
options.label: C
options.misconception: Applies the emptying pattern of a less restrictive outlet to an experimentally narrowed outlet.

options.text: Stable ejection load; stable residual volume
options.explanation: Maintaining filling and contraction strength does not neutralize outlet narrowing. The intervention independently raises the opposing load and thereby changes the volume left after ejection.
options.label: D
options.misconception: Assumes that matched filling and contraction strength prevent outlet narrowing from changing afterload.

options.text: Higher ejection load; greater residual volume
options.explanation: A narrower semilunar outlet raises the load against which the ventricle ejects. At unchanged filling and contractility, emptying falls and more volume remains after contraction.
options.label: E
options.misconception: No misconception: a narrower outlet raises ejection load and increases residual volume at fixed contraction strength.

context: Learning objective: Infer the effect of semilunar stenosis on afterload and residual ventricular volume. A narrower semilunar outlet raises the load against which the ventricle ejects. At unchanged filling and contractility, emptying falls and more volume remains after contraction.
